title: Six SOS negative vectors lack cbor_hex/machine drivability so rejection contract unenforced by CI
description: File: test/vectors/sos_cbor.json. Four non-finite entries embed hex only inside prose encoding_note; two range entries have cbor_payload but no cbor_hex. Automated consumers filter cbor_hex-less entries (rust tests sos_cbor_vectors.rs:22-24 assert driven==5; python test_vector_consumers_lci.py:276 same) leaving new contract ad-hoc-only verified. Add proper hex fields + extend consumer drivers.
close_reason: All six negative sos_cbor.json vectors now carry real cbor_hex computed with independent cbor2 encoder (schema key order type/node/ts/lat/lon/msg/seq; full node/ts constants matching positive vectors): four non-finite entries assembled with explicit raw IEEE-754 tokens 0xf97e00 f16 NaN lat / 0xf97c00 f16 +Inf lon / 0xfaff800000 f32 -Inf lat / 0xfb7ff8000000000000 f64 qNaN lon each paired with a valid opposite coordinate plus cbor_length 89/89/91/95; two range entries cbor_hex equals cbor2.dumps of their already-committed payloads, length 82. All six verified programmatically against the generator output byte-for-byte. Rust driver sos_cbor_vectors.rs branches on expected.decode_success:false asserting Err(InvalidValue) per vector and count assertion raised 5->11; canonical five positive vectors remain byte-stable (git diff shows zero removed lines). Python filter path verified empirically: range-entry hexes were picked up automatically by unchanged _sos_payload_cases and pass; the four JSON-unrepresentable payloadless hexes KeyError'd as predicted risk, handled minimally: wire-contract test now asserts raw structural properties for rejection cases, canonical-signing roundtrip skips them honestly (visible skips), and new test_sos_cbor_negative_vectors_rejected drives every negative vector's committed bytes through CheckInResource.render_post expecting BAD_REQUEST with nothing stored.
